name: Glycerol
aliases: E422, glycerol, glycerine, glycerin, glicerina, glicerol
what_is: A clear, viscous polyol liquid used as a humectant and sweetener.
why_botia: Glycerol attracts and retains water, which is why it keeps baked goods and gummies moist. In the European Union, since 2023, food E422 must be obtained only from vegetable oils and fats. In other markets, other authorised production routes exist and the label does not state which one was used, so outside the EU the source may still remain unresolved.
can_1: Detect E422 or Glycerol/Glycerine on scanned labels.
can_2: Explain that in the European Union food E422 must come from vegetable oils and fats, and keep the Animal and Muslim layers only for markets where the source may still be undeclared.
cannot_1: Determine the production route or source outside the European Union when the label does not state it.
cannot_2: Detect 3-MCPD contaminants above the 0.1 mg/kg limit.

title: Glycerol
description: Glycerol (E422) is a humectant and sweetener. In the European Union, since 2023, food E422 must come from vegetable oils and fats; outside the EU the source may still be undeclared.
robot_questions: How can I tell whether glycerine/glycerol on a label is of animal or plant origin?
Can a product presented as "dairy free" contain animal-derived glycerol?
robot_answers: In the European Union, since 2023, food-grade E422 can only be obtained from vegetable oils and fats. Other markets authorise other production methods, and the label does not say which was used, so there only the manufacturer can confirm the origin.

Outside the European Union, yes: "dairy free" means without dairy ingredients, not necessarily without animal-derived ingredients. In the EU, since 2023, food-grade E422 must come from vegetable oils and fats.
